target: popover modes, presentation state and light-dismiss boundaries
observed_behavior: The HTML Standard specifies popover auto, manual and hint attribute states. Auto popovers may close other unrelated auto popovers when shown and respond to close requests and light dismiss; manual popovers do not implicitly close others or respond to light dismiss/close requests; hint popovers can displace other hints without automatically displacing auto popovers. Its showPopover()/hidePopover()/togglePopover() algorithms govern top-layer presentation and visibility states, and outside pointer interactions light-dismiss only eligible auto/hint popovers under the defined algorithm.
context: W07 B2 K3 read-only observation; WHATWG HTML Living Standard authoritative for the described native HTML mechanisms and guarded algorithms only; source shows Last Updated 20 July 2026.
limitations: Popover is an HTML presentation/visibility mechanism; it is not by itself a dialog, tooltip, accessible role or modal-background inertness guarantee.
Attribute state depends on enumerated parsing rules: empty value maps to auto, invalid value to manual, and missing attribute to no-popover.
Auto/hint dismissal is algorithmic and conditional; manual popovers are intentionally excluded from automatic light-dismiss behavior.
Nested/related popover stack handling follows topmost-popover-ancestor algorithms, not a simplistic close-all guarantee.
No browser support, rendering, focus/AT behavior or user-task effectiveness was measured.
